correctness.rationale: For every coordinate edge, h changes by at most 3/2, proving B bounded. At any fixed vertex the central binomial summand has h=0 for all sufficiently large n and its weighted value is asymptotic to 2^(-i-j) sqrt(2n/pi). The finite-difference functional has exact polynomial (1-z)^3(1+z)^n; Parseval and Euler beta integration give the exact coefficient square sum 120*C(2n,n)/((n+1)(n+2)(n+3)). Cauchy-Schwarz yields central l1 decay 2^n O(n^-5/4); Hoeffding gives angular-tail l1 ≤16*2^n*exp(-2n/25), overcoming the at-most exp((n+3)/200) weight penalty. The resulting dual norm is O(n^-1/4)+O(n exp(-3n/40)) and tends to zero for every listed Banach space. This nonzero functional excludes a dense orbit. Embedded integer tests check identities n=0..200 but do not substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary source states the necessary individual binomial criterion and explicitly leaves its sufficiency on the full quadrant open. Its stated upper/lower exponential conditions neither imply nor forbid the constructed nonradial critical weight. The 2026 source public description treats the infinite quadrant under radial weighted Hilbert-space hypotheses; the example is exponentially nonradial, and its scalar cancellation does not follow by reducing to a radial weight. Related published record searches returned no equivalent theorem; highly relevant accessible original full text was read, with remaining full-text uncertainty of the 2026 preprint expressly retained.

value.rationale: This supplies a concrete negative answer to an explicitly published sufficiency problem for the infinite quadrant. It isolates a structural missing condition—collective cancellation among binomial rows—that survives even when every individual necessary norm grows without bound, with smooth bounded nearest-neighbor weight ratios. It is a genuine nonradial extension beyond the 2026 radial Hilbert-space setting and helps delimit plausible future joint Pascal-transfer criteria.
